## The reading, re-verified at source by the seat on `origin/main` `272a53066` at 2026-09-18T20:30Z

| link in the chain | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the declaration | `packages/types/src/data.ts:1214` — `sort?: Array<{ field: string; direction?: 'asc' \| 'desc' }>`: optional, and it gives an **empty array no meaning to distinguish** |
| the one receiving implementation | `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:4654` — `if (request.sort && request.sort.length > 0)` ⇒ `[]` takes the same branch as absent |
| the wire | the dev's runtime probe: `url(sort: [])` and `url(no sort key)` are **byte-identical**; the declared-array control differs (`&orderby=name%3Adesc`) — so the instrument can tell them apart and these two really are the same request |

⭐ The **ablation is what makes this a reading rather than an opinion**: the repair was written, proven on disk by blob hash, and its effect measured on **both** ends — at the sender the authored value goes `[]` → `undefined` (so the two implementations DO disagree on this input), and at the wire nothing moves. Restore proved by hash equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`. ⇒ the repair is observable exactly where it cannot matter.

## ⛔ Two things this card says that do not survive measurement

- ⛔ **「an array of retired string `sort` entries」 is not the only shape, and the retired SCALAR never reaches that filter.** `sort: 'name asc'` fails `Array.isArray`, so the export path already passes `sort: undefined`.
- ⛔ **「instead of omitting the key」 is not what either side does.** The request literal **always** carries a `sort` key — it is `undefined` when nothing is authored. The difference is `[]` vs `undefined`, and at the wire the parameter is already absent in both worlds.

## ⭐ Where the user-visible loss actually is — filed as its own card

The dev's probe, one run, three legs: the retired **scalar** string is refused **out loud** (1 diagnostic), the **array-of-strings** spelling is dropped with **0 diagnostics**, and the declared array works. `packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts:66` argues in its own docblock against exactly that silence — 「those into a row order that quietly stopped applying」 (seat-verified; control: `retired` on 7 lines of that file). ⇒ **objectui#9955**, class (a), same input one layer up.

⛔ Two things deliberately NOT filed, with reasons: the same filter shape in `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:3462`–`:3466` is the same measured no-op (a card for it would be a second no-op card), and the 「omit the empty container」 consistency residue re-files the card being closed.

Closing `not_planned`: there is nothing to repair here, and the successor for the real defect is named above.
